thread:
Sara Li: quick intake — bringing up `open-jx-6b-gguf` on infra2. Goal: pick a quantization profile that hits <=2.0x token-cost reduction without >2% delta on our conv+qa eval suite. propose smoke matrix: fp32 baseline -> int8 (perchannel symmetric) -> fp8 (hybrid e5-like) -> gguf hybrid (kv-cache cache-friendly).

Ajay Rao: sg. do we have a small calibration set that matches convo vs qa?

Sara Li: yes — `calib-mini/conv_qa_2k.jsonl` (2k prompts), split 1k conv / 1k qa. start with that for calibration and early QA.

Priya Kapoor: plan for evals: I can run SQuAD-like and our conv-turn-taking eval. Need a latency/cost report too. Which batch sizes?

Sara Li: run for batch sizes [1,4,8] for latency tail numbers and run throughput at 32/64 for cost sim. capture token/sec and p99 latency.

Jorge Mendes: add a quick hallucination/regression check: run 200 examples from our harmfulness/regression set. If >2% failure drop, mark as fail and try different scale/clip.

Ajay Rao: question — how aggressive for clipping/scaling in int8? we saw 0.02 clip for previous models worked but this arch might need 0.01.

Sara Li: start with 0.02 then 0.01 if quality fails. capture per-layer activation histos.

quant-ci-bot: CI job queued: `quant-smoke/1719994321` — will provision a T4 and run calib -> int8 -> fp8 -> gguf-hybrid. ETA ~ 40m.

Priya Kapoor: quick note: for fp8 use dynamic exponent format (E4M3-ish) in our runner variant. Past runs show better keyword fidelity.

Jorge Mendes: can we try transferring an existing calibration profile from `mosaic-7b` to this model as a quick probe? curious if profile transfer reduces calibration runs.

Sara Li: yes include transfer probe: two conditions: fresh calib vs transferred calib. Label results `transfer.yes` / `transfer.no`.

Ajay Rao: minor infra ask: pin `--kv-cache=on` for gguf hybrid runs, otherwise caching differences will skew cost.

Priya Kapoor: running evals now. kicking off:

```
run_eval --model open-jx-6b.gguf --quant int8 --calib calib-mini/conv_qa_2k.jsonl --batch 1 --out /tmp/171999_eval_int8.json
```

Priya Kapoor: result (smoke): int8 per-channel symmetric => 1.9x token-cost, conv+qa delta ~1.6% BLEU-style / EM. latency p99 batch=1: 210ms (baseline fp32 170ms). passing threshold for quality but p99 high.

Jorge Mendes: fp8 run queued.

quant-ci-bot: fp8 run complete — artifacts: s3://redwood-quant/artifacts/1719994321/fp8-report.json

Priya Kapoor: fp8 (E4M3) => 2.6x token-cost reduction, conv+qa delta 2.8% (just over threshold). hallucination/regression failures 1.1% (within), but QA EM drop too big.

Ajay Rao: interesting — cost benefit good but quality hit for QA. can we try mixed strategy: int8 for feed-forward, fp8 for attention?

Sara Li: add `hybrid-attn-fp8` variant to matrix. also try gguf hybrid with transferred calib.

Jorge Mendes: transfer calib probe finished: transferred profile gave similar cost but improved QA EM by ~0.9% compared to fresh int8. looks promising for profile reuse.

Priya Kapoor: decision proposal: promote int8 per-channel as default for now (meets quality + cost). keep fp8 as experimental with task-gated rollout (only conv-heavy workloads). test hybrid-attn-fp8 next sprint.

Ajay Rao: :thumbsup: agree. who owns follow-ups?

Sara Li: Priya -> full eval sweep + latency/cost dashboard PR. Ajay -> run hybrid-attn-fp8 kernels + per-layer clip tuning. Jorge -> create transfer-calib RFC and run across 3 other small models. I'll file rollout ticket and add to roadmap.

Priya Kapoor: noted, will upload full results and dashboards to the thread when ready.

Jorge Mendes: creating RFC draft now. ping me if you want quick checks.

Sara Li: thanks team — good smoke. will post summary in eng-ml channel and tag perf/infra for any kernel regressions. :sparkles:
